We trained X-WIN with 371,951 frontal and lateral CXRs from MIMIC-CXR [26] and 32,371 chest CT scans from the NLST [14].

capability_assessments.rationale: The evaluated reconstruction configuration renders projections from explicitly angle-conditioned predicted features. This is successor-view L2. The classification experiments alone evaluate representation utility. Generating several angles for tomography is not a reported matched action-comparison experiment supporting L3, and neither the training optimizer nor codebook tuning is a model-coupled clinical planner supporting L4.

scope.endpoint: CT-derived projection rendering and reconstruction fidelity

scope.population: Actual CXRs in the reported official VinDr test set
scope.endpoint: Representation-centroid alignment, not diagnostic or patient benefit
scope.split_evidence: Official VinDr test set explicitly identified
scope.limits: No certification of patient-level overlap controls, test-set non-reuse or locked-model external diagnostic validation. No R2 is inferred from synthetic NLST projections.

gate_assessments.rationale: Datasets and training image/scan counts are reported, but complete partitions, patient overlap, pretraining/downstream leakage controls, reconstruction split and hyperparameter-selection separation are not sufficiently documented. This is an evidence gap, not a demonstrated leakage failure.

Implemented action-conditioned successor-view prediction and reported rendering fidelity support acquisition L2. A gate pass is withheld because the reconstruction evaluation reference/split is incompletely specified and the required feature-assertion layer is intentionally omitted from this submission. No clinical-time prediction claim is evaluated.

The selected default-model scope is direct target-angle prediction, not multi-time forecasting or recursive planning. Multiple independently queried projection angles and the step-wise pretraining ablation do not supply an evaluated error-versus-rollout-horizon protocol. No effective clinical horizon is claimed.

No predictive probability/interval guarantee or uncertainty-dependent decision is claimed for the angle-conditioned rendering pipeline. Random target-angle sampling, contrastive temperature and VQ codebook usage are not predictive uncertainty calibration.

Angle role, unit, bounds, discretization and predictor conditioning are described and rendering is evaluated. Complete acquisition geometry, reconstruction angle protocol, context-specific support and the feature-assertion layer remain incomplete. Table 3 compares training designs, not same-origin clinical intervention effects.

No therapeutic-effect estimand or causal treatment benefit is claimed for the evaluated outputs. Geometric projection control around fixed anatomy is not a treatment-effect claim. This does not certify general causal validity.

The inspected pipeline performs representation learning, classification and rendering, without a model-coupled action optimizer or learned decision policy. AdamW training and decoder/hyperparameter selection are not planning.

This scoped profile excludes patient-facing advice, physical acquisition actuation and live workflow decisions. Consequently a live-action fail-behavior release gate is not applicable here. It would become required for clinical or device use; no safety-readiness claim follows.

Multiple downstream datasets and readout adaptation are reported, but independent-cohort overlap controls, exact splits, adaptation details and relevant subgroup/shift tests are incomplete. Cross-dataset transfer capability is not equivalent to an external clinical validation pass.

Actual VinDr test CXRs are used for centroid alignment and qualitative correspondences, but matched simulated/real successor outcomes or policy agreement are not evaluated. No actual-human reader/use study is reported. The demonstrated alignment diagnostic does not pass a sim-to-real utility or human-evaluation gate.

The scoped research contribution does not report realized prospective workflow or patient benefit. A prospective utility gate cannot be passed or failed by the offline classification/reconstruction endpoints.

The paper states research-code availability, not release for a defined operational clinical use. Operational authorization, monitoring, change control and release governance would require a new intended-use assessment.

legacy_cells.EI: Non-WM baselines included I-JEPA, DINOv2, RAD-DINO, CheXFound, Ark+, and vision-language models. On linear probing, X-WIN ViT-Large average AUROC was 0.892 versus 0.863 for Ark+.

legacy_cells.EL: The reconstructed CT volumes showed blurriness and loss of local details.
legacy_cells.FL: ViT context encoder maps a routine frontal or lateral radiograph to latent patches; an action-conditioned view predictor maps the latent representation and source-rotation angle to target-view latent patches; an EMA target encoder supplies CT-derived projection targets. Masked-image and domain-adaptation branches train the representations. Downstream linear-probe/fine-tuning heads perform CXR classification. No planner is described.
legacy_cells.FM: X-WIN distills 3D CT anatomical information into chest-radiograph representations by action-conditioned latent projection prediction, with affinity-guided alignment and structure-preserving adaptation to real CXRs.
legacy_cells.FN: Linear-probing average AUROC was 0.892 with ViT-Large and 0.883 with ViT-Base. Five-run COVIDx fine-tuning AUROC was 0.993 using all training data. Rendered-projection PSNR/SSIM were 30.23 dB/0.888, and reconstructed-CT PSNR/SSIM were 27.87 dB/0.789.
legacy_cells.FO: The discussion identifies remaining sim-to-real domain-adaptation challenges. Reconstructed volumes retained overall shape but had blurriness and loss of local detail.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors plan to explore invariant feature learning or domain-mapping strategies and compare performance with models trained directly on CT.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors state that existing CXR world models remain limited to 2D and do not embed 3D anatomical knowledge.
legacy_cells.FR: Demonstrated evidence is action-conditioned acquisition-view prediction, downstream representation performance, and reconstruction on retrospective datasets.
